newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy posts loss, fails to comply with loan agreement.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy posts loss, fails to comply with loan agreement.

text.p: Best Buy Co. Inc., the nation's largest retailer of electronics, personal computers and appliances, Wednesday reported a third-quarter loss largely due to the effects of PC price wars.
As a result, the company said it failed to comply with certain terms of a loan agreement with its bank lenders, which involves $271.5 million in borrowings as of Nov. 30.

Best Buy, which operates 272 stores in 32 states, posted a loss of about $11 million, or 25 cents a share, for the quarter ended Nov. 30, compared with profits of $17.8 million, or 41 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues rose to $2 billion from $1.9 billion.

The loss was largely due to a pre-tax charge of $15 million, or 21 cents a share, to write down personal computer inventories. This was mainly prompted by a drop in PC prices rather than excess levels of inventory, Best Buy said.
The Minneapolis-based company said it was in talks with its banks and expects to satisfactorily resolve the credit agreement.

Best Buy said its merchandise inventories fell to $1.85 billion as of Nov. 30 from $1.97 billion a year earlier, even though it added 21 new stores this year. This was almost entirely because the company reduced stocks of PCs in anticipation of new models equipped with Intel Corp.'s MMX microprocessor, which are expected after Jan. 1, it said.

Best Buy noted that new computers -- which were introduced in February in fiscal 1996 -- are being introduced six weeks earlier this fiscal year, causing computer prices to decline during the busiest months of the year.
Manufacturers and retailers were also promoting current models aggressively to make way for the new models, it added.

"The market for personal computers continues to be highly promotional with sizable price reductions, free merchandise and financing offers used to stimulate consumer demand," said Richard Schulze, Best Buy's chairman and chief executive.
"This resulted in extreme margin pressure beginning in November and continuing through December."
In addition, demand for consumer electronics and entertainment software has remained soft, further hurting sales and overall profitability, Schulze said.
Best Buy's stock fell 50 cents to $12 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
